questions.q: In a crontab line, what does "0 6 * * *" mean?
options: Run only on the 6th day of every month
Run at 6:00 a.m. every day
Run once, 6 hours after the crontab is saved
Run every 6 minutes
questions.explain: The fields are minute, hour, day, month, weekday — 0 and 6 with the rest as * means 6:00 a.m. daily.

questions.q: Why append ">> etl_run.log 2>&1" to a cron command?
options: It deletes the log file before each run
Cron runs with no terminal attached, so without redirecting output somewhere it is simply lost
It is required syntax for every cron line, regardless of logging
It makes the script run faster
questions.explain: 2>&1 sends error output to the same place as normal output, and >> appends both to the log file.

questions.q: What is the Windows Task Scheduler equivalent of a daily cron job?
options: There is no way to schedule a script on Windows
A scheduled task with a Daily trigger and an action that runs python.exe with the script's path as an argument
A registry key edited manually with regedit
A Windows service that must be written in C++
questions.explain: Task Scheduler's GUI (or the PowerShell cmdlets) create a trigger and an action, mirroring what cron does on Linux/macOS.

questions.q: Why might a script that reads "orders.csv" with a relative path work fine when run by hand but fail under cron or Task Scheduler?
options: The file gets renamed automatically when scheduled
Relative paths are never valid in Python
The scheduler starts the script from its own working directory, which is often not the folder the script lives in
cron and Task Scheduler cannot read CSV files at all
questions.explain: Using an absolute path, or one built from the script's own location, avoids this entirely.

questions.q: Why check both the scheduler's own log (e.g. cron's syslog entry) AND the pipeline's own log file?
options: They always contain identical information
The scheduler's log confirms the script was even launched, while the pipeline's log confirms whether it succeeded once running
Only the scheduler's log matters; the pipeline's log is redundant
Checking both is unnecessary if the script has no bugs
questions.explain: A script that never ran at all leaves an empty pipeline log rather than an error — the scheduler's log catches that case.
